claims.claim_vi: The source describes three processes: crawling (crawlers start from seed pages and follow links), indexing (extract keywords, content type, freshness, language and other signals into an index) and serving results (query analysis, retrieval from the index, ranking).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Own experiment, 2026-10-19, Python 3: synthetic web of 20,000 pages, 100 words each from a 2,000-word Zipf vocabulary, 2 to 8 links per page (70 percent to popular pages); breadth-first crawl from 3 seeds found pages per layer 3, 15, 76, 360, 1,658, 5,552, 7,446, 2,888, 481, 54, 5, 1; 18,539 of 20,000 reached, 1,461 unreachable.
claims.verified_by: Script run in the session with a fixed seed; results copied from output.

claims.claim_vi: Own experiment: with an inverted index of 2,000 terms, queries of two words matched 13,906, 280 and 18 pages; scanning every page took about 54.2, 69.0 and 66.4 ms and index intersection about 11.5, 1.1 and 0.2 ms on the session machine; a tf times idf style score ranks matches.

The scoring rule in the experiment is the author's simple choice and is not claimed to match any real engine.
